title: Every route declares who may call it, and one test holds each to it
description: Who may call a route is decided today by a Public flag in routes.go that the generated manifest does not show, and by checks written inside handlers. Media already requires a token (server.go requireAuth), but nothing pins it: one changed line opens a film to anyone, and TestProtectedRoutesRejectAnonymousRequests asks four routes. The owner's rule (2026-11-16) is that playback and personal data always require authorization, with no compatibility exception. This task makes the declaration explicit and required, prints it in compat/endpoints.yaml, documents it, and asks every route. No answer changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Route has Access, 'anyone' or 'viewer', in place of Public. A route with no Access fails go test ./internal/api naming the route, and Server.Handler() panics on it, so the binary does not start. An 'anyone' route has a non-empty Why and a 'viewer' route has none; a test fails on either. jellyscale --print-routes writes access: for every route and TestManifestIsCurrent holds compat/endpoints.yaml to it

The open list is pinned by a test that names it: GET /System/Info/Public, GET and POST /System/Ping, GET /Branding/Configuration, GET /Branding/Css, GET /Branding/Css.css, GET /QuickConnect/Enabled, GET /Users/Public, POST /Users/AuthenticateByName, and, by the owner's decision on pictures, GET /Items/{itemId}/Images/{imageType} and GET /Items/{itemId}/Images/{imageType}/{imageIndex}. The other 77 routes are 'viewer'. Adding or removing an open route fails the test until its list is changed

TestAccess (integration tier, Postgres, both stores, the synthetic films with a text subtitle, a font and chapter pictures) asks every route of Routes(), 88 or more, on a handler with roles api and stream, and each role's routes again on a handler with that role alone. Path wildcards are filled by name from the fixtures, and a wildcard the test has no value for fails it naming the route

For every 'viewer' route the answer is 401 with the body 'unauthorized' and under 64 bytes, with no Content-Range, Content-Disposition, ETag or Location header, for: no token; an unknown token in each of the seven spellings compat.ParseAuth reads (Authorization MediaBrowser, Authorization Emby, X-Emby-Authorization, X-Emby-Token, X-MediaBrowser-Token, ApiKey, api_key); a token signed out through POST /Sessions/Logout; the token of a user deleted from the users table. HEAD of each GET route and the path in upper case with a trailing slash answer the same
For every 'anyone' route the same requests answer neither 401 nor 403

With a valid token in each of the seven spellings, GET /Videos/{itemId}/stream?static=true with Range bytes=0-9 answers 206 with the film's first ten bytes, and every 'viewer' route answers as it does today: the unit, integration, roles, e2e and differential tiers pass with no test changed except the one this task replaces, and compat/differences.yaml gains no entry
The mux serves nothing outside Routes() except GET /healthz, GET /readyz, GET /web/ and GET /; a test fails on any other registered pattern

Forced, real processes (test/roles.sh: two api processes and a stream process): a token signed in through api 1 gets 206 for a byte range from stream; POST /Sessions/Logout through api 1 answers 204; the very next request with that token through api 2 (GET /Users/Me) and through stream (the byte range) answers 401, with no retry. Named mutant, which must fail every run: tokens remembered in the process for 5 seconds

Forced, the snapshot never decides while Postgres answers: a session reports Playing, the test waits until the stream replica's snapshot holds its token (the hook the outage tests use), the token is signed out, and its byte range answers 401. Named mutant, which must fail every run: a Snapshot route served from the snapshot before Postgres is asked

With Postgres held away (testenv.DBProxy): every 'viewer' route asked with no token answers 401 within 1 second; a Snapshot route asked with an unknown token sends no byte while Postgres is away and answers 401 once it is back
Named mutants, each failing TestAccess on every run: GET /Videos/{itemId}/{file} declared 'anyone'; the guard accepting any non-empty token; a new Route with an empty Access

docs/access.md (new, linked from README and DOMAINS.md) holds the model and one table row per served route: what it does, who it requires and its scope. A test fails when a route of compat/endpoints.yaml has no row, a row names no route, or a row's 'requires' cell differs from the manifest

DOMAINS.md gains a Security invariant: every route declares its access; none is open by default; media, item data and anything naming a user are never open; an open route says why. docs/status.md says a client must send its token on every media request and that this is stricter than Jellyfin on purpose. The sentence proposed for PRODUCT.md's compatibility policy is in the pull request's description, not in the file
notes: Owner, 2026-11-16: playback and personal data always require authorization; compatibility never means copying Jellyfin's openings. Media already answers 401 with no token, so this task changes no answer. 'admin' joins Access with its first route in JS-033. The draft's compat/anonymous.yaml is dropped: Route.Access is the one source. Pictures: jellyfin-web builds picture URLs with no token (web-dist/node_modules.jellyfin-apiclient.bundle.js, getImageUrl) and an cannot send one, so a token on pictures removes every poster; item ids are random (internal/library/scan.go). If the owner decides pictures need a token, that is its own task and the pinned list here has nine routes. Found while reading, for the backlog: two sign-ins at once with one DeviceId can leave two tokens for the device (users.go:107-117, no unique index on user_id, device_id); a viewer sees the worker's name in their own TranscodingInfo (transcoding_info.go:69-70). Owner's decisions (2026-11-16, on Fable 5.2's access model, .results/access-model-fable-2026-11-16.md): pictures by id open to whoever holds the id, by name need a token; per-library access right after JS-033; a revoked or disabled user's running stream stops within 15 s; a viewer sees no other viewer's name; an administrator manages accounts but never browses, plays or reports as another user; a Policy field jellyscale does not enforce is refused when changed (400); 'may download' is honoured; operator keys are never users; no issue is filed on Findroid for now.
